issues.description: The type of Person.birthday is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the template use java.time.LocalDate for Person.birthday, but the solution repository's common model defines birthday as a String. This discrepancy also leads to internal inconsistencies inside the solution (e.g. PersonScene treats birthday as LocalDate while Person model there is String), which would confuse students and may cause compile/runtime errors when they follow the exercise (DatePicker and service sorting expect LocalDate).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.birthday type consistent across all artifacts. Revert/adjust the solution's common model to use java.time.LocalDate for birthday (with matching getter/setter) so it matches the template and the UML in the problem statement, and ensure JSON (de)serialization is configured if necessary. Alternatively, if String is desired, update the problem statement, template code (DatePicker usage), and service logic to consistently use String everywhere—keeping the UI and sorting logic coherent.

issues.description: The concept 'birthday' for Person is represented inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the template's common Person model use java.time.LocalDate for the birthday attribute, but the solution's common Person model declares birthday as a String. Additionally, the solution's PersonScene UI code treats birthday as a LocalDate when interacting with a DatePicker. This mismatch (same conceptual attribute 'birthday' with different types/representations) creates a mapping barrier for students trying to connect the problem description, the provided template, and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of Person.birthday consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's common Person.birthday back to java.time.LocalDate and adjust serialization/deserialization accordingly so PersonScene (DatePicker) works directly with LocalDate, or (B) if using String is required, update the problem statement, template model, and UI code to use String consistently (with explicit conversion at UI boundaries). Prefer aligning to LocalDate to match the UML and reduce student confusion.
